sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯汀·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: The Camp Fire, one of the deadliest and the most destructive wildfires in California history, continues to rage in the state, as two other fires burn there simultaneously.
sentences.zh: “坎普”山火是加州历史上最致命、最具破坏性的野火之一，目前该州仍有两场火灾同时在燃烧，火势持续蔓延。

sentences.en: In a state where devastating wildfires were already the new normal, this time feels different.
sentences.zh: 在一个毁灭性野火已成“新常态”的州，这一次的感觉却有所不同。

sentences.en: November 12th.
Paradise is right in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada, about 100 miles north of Sacramento.
sentences.zh: 天堂镇位于内华达山脉的山脚下，在萨克拉门托以北约100英里处。

sentences.en: It has roots back in the old extraction economy days of the 1800s as a logging and mining town.
sentences.zh: 它起源于19世纪旧时代的资源开采经济，曾是一个伐木和采矿小镇。

sentences.en: But its real life in recent years has been partly as a retirement community and partly as an affordable place for people who don't have a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，它实际上既是一个退休社区，也是许多经济拮据者的廉价居住地。

sentences.en: It has a kind of working-class vibe.
sentences.zh: 它有一种工人阶级的氛围。

sentences.en: And I never saw it in the days before the fire, but it, by all accounts, was a beautiful place.
sentences.zh: 虽然我在火灾前从未去过那里，但据所有人说，那是一个美丽的地方。

sentences.en: Kirk Johnson is a national correspondent covering the WeSt. He spent the weekend in Paradise, California.
sentences.zh: 柯克·约翰逊是报道西部地区的全国记者。他周末在加州天堂镇度过。

sentences.en: Around 6.30 a.m.
sentences.zh: 大约早上6点30分。

sentences.en: on Thursday, it began in the hills near Paradise.
sentences.zh: 周四，火灾在天堂镇附近的山丘上开始了。

sentences.en: This is legit how dark it is in my car right now, and it is 10.23 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 这就是我现在车里有多黑，现在是早上10点23分。

sentences.en: And it's so smoky out that it looks like nighttime.
sentences.zh: 外面烟雾弥漫，看起来像晚上一样。

sentences.en: Like, I can't even see inside the house.
sentences.zh: 我甚至看不见房子里面。

sentences.en: I'm in my car right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在在车里。

sentences.en: We're loading up, and me and my mom are going to be meeting down at Kohl's in Chico.
sentences.zh: 我们正在装车，我和我妈打算在奇科的科尔百货见面。

sentences.en: And a kind of a firestorm roared through with a pace that no one there had ever witnessed or really foreseen, I think.
sentences.zh: 一场火风暴以一种我认为那里没人见过或预料到的速度席卷而来。

sentences.en: It's 11.39 in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 现在是下午11点39分。

sentences.en: The reason I can see is because of this fire.
sentences.zh: 我能看见是因为这场火。

sentences.en: It was something that could not be stopped.
sentences.zh: 这是无法阻挡的。

sentences.en: There's our homes down there.
sentences.zh: 我们的家就在下面。

sentences.en: All this is happening right now.
sentences.zh: 这一切正在发生。

sentences.en: It's 12.42 in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 现在是下午12点42分。

sentences.en: But all I see is smoke.
sentences.zh: 但我看到的只有烟。

sentences.en: Because it was sweeping through a populated area, 26,000 people in that valley, it was all about rescue and getting people out.
sentences.zh: 因为它席卷了人口稠密的地区，那个山谷里有26,000人，所以一切都关乎救援和撤离。

sentences.en: And there was no attempt or ability to even start to do anything about it until it was hours into the fire.
sentences.zh: 在火灾发生后的几个小时内，根本没有尝试或能力去采取任何措施。

sentences.en: So it all became about evacuation before it ever became about putting it out.
sentences.zh: 所以，在考虑灭火之前，一切都变成了撤离。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And evacuation from home was really, for many people, only the beginning of the ordeal and the horror.
sentences.zh: 对于许多人来说，从家中撤离实际上只是苦难和恐怖的开始。

sentences.en: We're on the road, and we're meters away.
sentences.zh: 我们在路上，离火只有几米远。

sentences.en: And we're all stuck on this road.
sentences.zh: 我们都被困在这条路上。

sentences.en: People's houses, and the fucking wind is bringing it over.
sentences.zh: 人们的房子，该死的风把火带过来了。

sentences.en: Why is it true?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: I wonder what the fuck they're going to do.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们到底要干什么。

sentences.en: There's one main highway in and out of Paradise.
sentences.zh: 进出天堂镇只有一条主干道。

sentences.en: I'm on Skyway on my way out right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在正走在撤离的天堂大道上。

sentences.en: Everything is on fire.
sentences.zh: 一切都在燃烧。

sentences.en: And it was choked with people escaping, but also fire closing in on both sides of the highway.
sentences.zh: 路上挤满了逃生的人，但公路两侧火势也在逼近。

sentences.en: Go!
sentences.zh: 快走！

sentences.en: People talked about and photographed and recorded at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时人们谈论、拍摄并记录下了这一切。

sentences.en: I hope my fucking car doesn't start on fire because I got this.
sentences.zh: 我希望我这辆该死的车别着火，因为我带着这个。

sentences.en: Is this fireproof?
sentences.zh: 这防火吗？

sentences.en: Bloody hope so.
sentences.zh: 但愿如此。

sentences.en: What's up with the lights?
sentences.zh: 灯怎么了？

sentences.en: People told me about getting into their cars, and the car died.
sentences.zh: 人们告诉我，他们上了车，结果车熄火了。

sentences.en: And the fire is closing in.
sentences.zh: 火正在逼近。

sentences.en: And they can see the fire, and they can see neighbors' homes on fire.
sentences.zh: 他们能看到火，也能看到邻居的房子在燃烧。

sentences.en: And suddenly they have no way out.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们无路可逃。

sentences.en: The window is so hot, I can't even touch the window right now.
sentences.zh: 窗户太烫了，我现在连碰都碰不了。

sentences.en: And one woman described going by a motorhome that had pulled off and was fully engulfed in flames.
sentences.zh: 一位女士描述说，她经过一辆停在路边并被火焰完全吞没的房车。

sentences.en: And the traffic ahead of them stopped with her vehicle right next to this burning motorhome.
sentences.zh: 她前面的车流停住了，她的车正好停在那辆燃烧的房车旁边。

sentences.en: And they couldn't get out, and the heat was coming through the glass of their car from the blazing motorhome.
sentences.zh: 他们无法离开，燃烧的房车发出的热量透过车窗玻璃传了进来。

sentences.en: And it felt like hours, she said, but it was probably, you know, a couple minutes, and they were able to get past it.
sentences.zh: 她说感觉过了几个小时，但其实可能也就几分钟，他们最终设法通过了。

sentences.en: Hey, guess what?
sentences.zh: 嘿，猜怎么着？

sentences.en: We're not going to catch on fire, okay?
sentences.zh: 我们不会着火的，好吗？

sentences.en: We're going to stay away from it.
sentences.zh: 我们会远离它的。

sentences.en: And we'll be just fine.
sentences.zh: 我们会没事的。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: We're doing all right.
sentences.zh: 我们没问题的。

sentences.en: Another guy told me they had gotten the signal that it was closing in when they started hearing propane tanks exploding in the neighborhood around them.
sentences.zh: 另一个人告诉我，当他们听到周围社区的丙烷罐爆炸时，他们收到了火势逼近的信号。

sentences.en: So they ran from their home.
sentences.zh: 于是他们逃离了家园。

sentences.en: This was a guy who didn't own a car, so they went onto the road on foot.
sentences.zh: 这个人没有车，所以他们步行上了路。

sentences.en: There was a young pregnant woman and eight people all together.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个年轻的孕妇，总共八个人。

sentences.en: And a guy in a pickup truck just pulled up next to them and screamed, get in the back.
sentences.zh: 一辆皮卡车停在他们旁边，司机大喊：“快上车斗！”

sentences.en: And they piled in and made it down.
sentences.zh: 他们挤了上去，成功逃了出来。

sentences.en: Oh, shit.
sentences.zh: 该死。

sentences.en: That's a tree that's on fire there.
sentences.zh: 那棵树着火了。

sentences.en: Oh, my.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Should I pray to God?
sentences.zh: 我该向上帝祈祷吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't know how to.
sentences.zh: 我不知道怎么祈祷。

sentences.en: Shirley's praying right now.
sentences.zh: 雪莉正在祈祷。

sentences.en: There was just one story after another that was impossible to forget.
sentences.zh: 一个接一个的故事，让人无法忘怀。

sentences.en: By the time I drove up Skyline, it had been 48 hours since that mass escape, and the smoke was intensely thick still.
sentences.zh: 当我开车上天际线公路时，距离那场大逃亡已经过去了48小时，烟雾依然浓重。

sentences.en: The ash was still falling from the sky, and ash coated everything that had been airborne and still laying down a layer of ash.
sentences.zh: 灰烬仍在从天而降，覆盖了所有曾经悬浮在空中并沉降下来的东西。

sentences.en: The power lines and power poles were down across portions of the road, and then vehicles that had burned to the metal frames and glass and melted things everywhere.
sentences.zh: 电线和电线杆横倒在路面上，到处都是烧得只剩下金属框架和玻璃的车辆，还有融化的东西。

sentences.en: And it was impossible for me not to just stop sometimes and look at a scene and try and imagine what had unfolded there when you would go by a school bus.
sentences.zh: 我忍不住停下来看着这些场景，试图想象当你经过一辆校车时，那里发生了什么。

sentences.en: And it was, you know, completely gutted by flame, you know, what had happened there, who had been in that bus, and where did they go, and how did they get out?
sentences.zh: 它被火焰完全烧毁了，你知道，那里发生了什么，车里是谁，他们去了哪里，又是怎么逃出来的？

sentences.en: Kirk, how many people do we know to have died in this fire at this point, as we're talking on Sunday afternoon?
sentences.zh: 柯克，截至周日下午，我们知道这场火灾中有多少人死亡？

sentences.en: It's still a running tally, so we don't know where it's going to end up.
sentences.zh: 这还是一个变动的数字，所以我们不知道最终会是多少。

sentences.en: But based on where we are, it looks like it will be the third most deadly in lives lost, but most destructive in terms of homes and businesses and communities destroyed.
sentences.zh: 但就目前的情况来看，这似乎是死亡人数第三多的火灾，但在房屋、企业和社区损毁方面却是最具破坏性的。

sentences.en: And that's because this fire, it sounds like, behaved in a way that despite the history of wildfires in California, was somehow unlike anything before it?
sentences.zh: 听起来这场火灾的表现方式，尽管加州有野火历史，却以某种方式不同于以往任何火灾？

sentences.en: The general nature of fires, they don't burn generally every single thing.
sentences.zh: 火灾的普遍性质通常不会烧毁所有东西。

sentences.en: They seek out the fuels that are handy in a way and drawn toward those.
sentences.zh: 它们会寻找手边易燃的燃料，并被吸引过去。

sentences.en: But if there's a new normal that is feared, it's the kind of fire-like campfire that is sort of monolithic in kind of sweeping the slate.
sentences.zh: 但如果说有一种令人恐惧的“新常态”，那就是像“坎普”山火这样，以一种近乎整体性的方式横扫一切。

sentences.en: And that's really raised a lot of anxieties about what the future might hold.
sentences.zh: 这确实引发了人们对未来可能发生什么的许多焦虑。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So these fires burn everything.
sentences.zh: 所以这些火灾烧毁了一切。

sentences.en: They don't hop around.
sentences.zh: 它们不会跳跃。

sentences.en: They don't skip a tree or a house.
sentences.zh: 它们不会放过一棵树或一所房子。

sentences.en: They just consume everything.
sentences.zh: 它们只是吞噬一切。

sentences.en: There were huge stretches of that very pattern in Paradise.
sentences.zh: 天堂镇有大片地区呈现出这种模式。

sentences.en: It didn't seem to leave anything standing, or its pace and its heat and its ferocity was such that it didn't pick and choose and it just swept.
sentences.zh: 它似乎没有留下任何东西，它的速度、热量和凶猛程度使得它不加选择，直接横扫而过。

sentences.en: So more or less, the town of Paradise was destroyed this weekend.
sentences.zh: 所以，天堂镇这个周末基本上被摧毁了。

sentences.en: That is about what you have to say.
sentences.zh: 你不得不这么说。

sentences.en: The cumulative impact is really going to be either the end of that community or a moment to think about rebuilding it entirely.
sentences.zh: 累积的影响要么是该社区的终结，要么是一个考虑彻底重建的时刻。

sentences.en: There was very little that looked like, well, here's a place where you can kind of start over and go back.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有什么地方看起来像是可以重新开始并回去的地方。

sentences.en: The assumption by survivors and former residents is that the place is gone and that they have nothing left to go back to there.
sentences.zh: 幸存者和前居民的假设是，这个地方已经消失了，他们回去后一无所有。

sentences.en: And how has the federal government responded to the campfire and to what's happening right now in California?
sentences.zh: 联邦政府对“坎普”山火以及加州目前发生的事情有何回应？

sentences.en: I'm going to start out with the most current numbers.
sentences.zh: 我先从最新的数字开始说起。

sentences.en: The federal government has responded as it always has for emergencies of this sort.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府像往常处理此类紧急情况一样做出了回应。

sentences.en: Total firefighters assigned to the fire right now, 32-23.
sentences.zh: 目前分配到火灾现场的消防员总数为3223人。

sentences.en: The personnel and the coordination and the promise of funding has been there.
sentences.zh: 人员、协调和资金承诺都已经到位。

sentences.en: There's more than 7,000 firefighters out on the fire lines still.
sentences.zh: 仍有超过7000名消防员在火线上工作。

sentences.en: But many of those assumptions were sort of upended on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 但周六，许多假设被推翻了。

sentences.en: President Trump is responding to the fires burning in California right now.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统正在回应加州目前燃烧的火灾。

sentences.en: When President Trump tweeted that...
sentences.zh: 当特朗普总统发推文说……

sentences.en: There's no reason for these massive, deadly and costly forest fires in California.
sentences.zh: 加州这些大规模、致命且代价高昂的森林火灾没有理由发生。

sentences.en: There were mismanagement issues of the forests in play in California.
sentences.zh: 加州的森林管理存在问题。

sentences.en: Billions of dollars are given each year with so many lives lost, all because of gross mismanagement of the forests.
sentences.zh: 每年投入数十亿美元，却造成如此多的人员伤亡，完全是因为森林管理不善。

sentences.en: Remedy now or no more Fed payments?
sentences.zh: 现在补救，否则停止联邦拨款？

sentences.en: And that really hit a raw nerve for people who were still reeling from it.
sentences.zh: 这确实触动了那些仍在痛苦中挣扎的人们的神经。

sentences.en: That statement was idiotic.
sentences.zh: 那份声明是愚蠢的。

sentences.en: It was ill-timed.
sentences.zh: 时机不对。

sentences.en: And it's ignorant.
sentences.zh: 而且很无知。

sentences.en: In fearing that the federal response or the future response was somehow in doubt.
sentences.zh: 人们担心联邦的应对或未来的应对措施是否会受到质疑。

sentences.en: Look, I don't think it's a gross exaggeration to say Trump's declared war on California.
sentences.zh: 听着，我认为说特朗普向加州宣战并不算夸张。

sentences.en: Governor-elect Gavin Newsom immediately and vehemently denounced the president's tweet.
sentences.zh: 当选州长加文·纽森立即强烈谴责了总统的推文。

sentences.en: He said that this is not a time for partisanship.
sentences.zh: 他说现在不是搞党派之争的时候。

sentences.en: So clearly interpreted the president's statement as a politically driven rather than land management or environmental policy statement.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，他将总统的声明解读为政治驱动的，而非土地管理或环境政策声明。

sentences.en: And presumably politically driven at a democratically dominated state.
sentences.zh: 而且大概是针对民主党占主导地位的州进行的政治驱动。

sentences.en: That is certainly how you would read Gavin's statement.
sentences.zh: 这当然是你解读加文声明的方式。

sentences.en: And President Trump is suggesting that these fires are the fault of mismanagement, presumably by the state of California.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统暗示这些火灾是管理不善造成的，大概是指加州政府。

sentences.en: Is that what people think he's saying?
sentences.zh: 人们认为他是在这么说吗？

sentences.en: That appears to be the suggestion that the state of California was somehow at fault in managing those lands.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是在暗示加州政府在管理这些土地方面负有某种责任。

sentences.en: But the fact is that the vast majority of forest lands in California, like most of the West, are federal.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，加州绝大多数的森林土地，就像西部大部分地区一样，都是联邦所有的。

sentences.en: Well, the community of paradise itself really backs up to a national foreSt.
sentences.zh: 天堂镇本身确实背靠国家森林。

sentences.en: And those are not state policies at all.
sentences.zh: 那些根本不是州政策。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国。

sentences.en: Forest Service defines and manages those lands for better or worse.
sentences.zh: 林务局定义并管理这些土地，无论好坏。

sentences.en: And there are definitely people who believe federal forest management has not been exactly what it should be either.
sentences.zh: 当然也有人认为联邦森林管理也并不完全如人意。

sentences.en: Well, and also, how much of this, as far as we understand it, does have to do with forest management versus, say, climate change?
sentences.zh: 那么，据我们了解，这在多大程度上与森林管理有关，又在多大程度上与气候变化有关？

sentences.en: That's a hard mix to try and parse out.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难区分的复杂问题。

sentences.en: Certainly, there are many areas in the West and in California where decades of fire suppression, when a fire starts in a forest, you try and put it out.
sentences.zh: 当然，西部和加州的许多地区，几十年来一直实行灭火政策，即当森林起火时，你试图扑灭它。

sentences.en: That's been the ethos and the mantra since, you know, the Smokey Bear days.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这从“斯莫基熊”时代起就是一种信条和口号。

sentences.en: And there's also a lot less logging in a lot of those areas that people have said reduces the fuel load that can burn in a fire.
sentences.zh: 而且在许多人认为能减少火灾燃料负荷的地区，伐木活动也减少了很多。

sentences.en: So it may be that it kind of comes from both sides if the forest is less healthy at a time when the environment around it is also changing and drying and whatever,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果森林在环境不断变化、变得干燥的同时，健康状况也在下降，那么这可能就是双重因素共同作用的结果，

sentences.en: it gets hit from both sides.
sentences.zh: 它受到了两方面的打击。

sentences.en: So fire suppression, combined with less logging, may leave these forests primed for fires, and climate change may do the reSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，消防抑制措施加上伐木减少，可能让这些森林更容易起火，而气候变化则完成了剩下的部分。

sentences.en: In that sense, the president has a point about the need to manage these forests.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，总统关于需要管理这些森林的观点是有道理的。

sentences.en: But in fact, it sounds like you're saying, Kirk, that that's really the job of his own federal government, more than the state of California,
sentences.zh: 但事实上，柯克，听起来你是在说，这其实更多是他自己的联邦政府的工作，而不是加利福尼亚州政府的工作，

sentences.en: that he's just threatened to withhold funds from.
sentences.zh: 而他刚刚威胁要扣留给加州的资金。

sentences.en: Well, if it comes back down to who owns the land, then yeah, you can only hold the state of California responsible for what it's responsible for.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果归根结底要看土地归谁所有，那么是的，你只能让加利福尼亚州对其负责的事务承担责任。

sentences.en: And like most Western states, the federal government is a giant presence on the land, whether it's in Forest Service or Bureau of Land Management or Fish and Wildlife.
sentences.zh: 而且像大多数西部州一样，联邦政府在土地上有着巨大的存在感，无论是林务局、土地管理局还是鱼类及野生动物管理局。

sentences.en: It's a huge cumulative force that either does its job well or doesn't.
sentences.zh: 这是一股巨大的累积力量，它要么把工作做好，要么做不好。

sentences.en: And Kirk, as we speak on Sunday afternoon, the campfire, which destroyed so much of Paradise, is just one of the three fires that are still burning in California.
sentences.zh: 柯克，就在我们周日下午交谈时，“坎普”山火（Camp Fire）——那场摧毁了“天堂镇”大部分地区的火灾——只是加州目前仍在燃烧的三场火灾之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The campfire became the focus, and in the huge numbers of homes and businesses destroyed and lives lost, that sort of focal point of the fires.
sentences.zh: “坎普”山火成了焦点，由于大量房屋和企业被毁，生命丧失，它成了这些火灾的中心点。

sentences.en: But it's really a fire moment in a totally catastrophic and really, I guess, coincidental way.
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一个以一种完全灾难性且非常、我想说是巧合的方式发生的火灾时刻。

sentences.en: I mean, environmental forces are always interconnected, but the campfire began early in the morning on Thursday, and seven hours later,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，环境力量总是相互关联的，但“坎普”山火是在周四清晨开始的，七小时后，

sentences.en: the Woolsey Fire began in Southern California.
sentences.zh: 伍尔西（Woolsey）山火在南加州开始了。

sentences.en: And in a state where something like that is coming from both ends at you, starting in the same day, it's a collective trauma rather than, you know, one big, bad disaster.
sentences.zh: 在一个同一天内两头受敌的州，这是一种集体创伤，而不是那种单一的、严重的灾难。

sentences.en: You know, ever since the officials in California started using this phrase, new normal, I've struggled to understand how anyone could possibly embrace that concept,
sentences.zh: 你知道，自从加州的官员开始使用“新常态”这个词以来，我就一直难以理解怎么会有人接受这个概念，

sentences.en: that at any moment in California, no matter what season of the year it is, your home, your neighbor's home, your town hall, your post office could just be destroyed by fire,
sentences.zh: 即在加州的任何时刻，无论是一年中的哪个季节，你的家、你邻居的家、你的市政厅、你的邮局都可能被大火摧毁，

sentences.en: as if that is somehow normal at all.
sentences.zh: 就好像这在某种程度上是正常的。

sentences.en: I think it's, yeah, it's an impossible thing to get your head around it.
sentences.zh: 我想，是的，这让人难以接受。

sentences.en: It's like living in the present.
sentences.zh: 这就像活在当下。

sentences.en: We all say we want to do it, but it's very difficult to do, and it's impossible and probably not good for your mental health to walk around all the time thinking that your town,
sentences.zh: 我们都说想做到这一点，但这非常困难，而且整天想着你的城镇、

sentences.en: your home, your community is on the sword's edge or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你的家、你的社区正处于刀尖上或类似境地，这不仅是不可能的，对心理健康也可能没有好处。

sentences.en: So I think there's a lot of natural human denial that there is a new normal.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，人们在很大程度上有一种否认“新常态”的自然心理。

sentences.en: It's much easier to and tempting to want to look back and say that things will look more like they have in the past, and we have dealt with bad things in the past, and we're tough.
sentences.zh: 回顾过去，说事情会变得像过去一样，说我们过去处理过糟糕的事情，我们很坚强，这要容易得多，也更诱人。

sentences.en: And so how a new normal sinks into ordinary people is, I think, a tough road of its own that hasn't gotten there yet.
sentences.zh: 所以，“新常态”如何深入普通人的内心，我认为这本身就是一条艰难的路，目前还没走到那一步。

sentences.en: Kirk, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 柯克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: By Sunday night, the campfire had matched the deadliest in California history with 29 fatalities.
sentences.zh: 到周日晚上，“坎普”山火已造成29人死亡，追平了加州历史上最致命火灾的纪录。

sentences.en: Seven of the victims in the town of Paradise died in their vehicles.
sentences.zh: 天堂镇的遇难者中有七人死在车里。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Joining us now from Naples, Florida, Governor Scott, who thought he won election to the Senate Tuesday night.
sentences.zh: 现在加入我们的是来自佛罗里达州那不勒斯的斯科特州长，他本以为自己在周二晚上的参议院选举中获胜了。

sentences.en: Florida has begun the first full statewide recount of votes in its history, after results from Tuesday's midterms left the elections for governor and U.S.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州已经开始了其历史上首次全州范围的选票重新计票，此前周二中期选举的结果使得州长和美国

sentences.en: Senate too close to call.
sentences.zh: 参议院的选举结果过于接近，无法宣布获胜者。

sentences.en: In the Senate race, Republican Rick Scott's lead over the Democratic incumbent, Bill Nelson, has slipped to 12,600 votes.
sentences.zh: 在参议院竞选中，共和党人里克·斯科特的领先优势相对于民主党现任议员比尔·纳尔逊已缩减至12600票。

sentences.en: Well, we had 8 million people vote.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们有800万人投票。

sentences.en: Chuck Schumer spent over $50 million trying to beat me, but we won.
sentences.zh: 查克·舒默花了超过5000万美元试图击败我，但我们赢了。

sentences.en: In the governor's race, Andrew Gillum, the Democrat, is behind about 33,000 votes and has retracted his earlier concession to his Republican opponent, Ron DeSantis.
sentences.zh: 在州长竞选中，民主党人安德鲁·吉勒姆落后约33000票，并撤回了他早先对共和党对手罗恩·德桑蒂斯的让步。

sentences.en: I am replacing my words of concession with an uncompromised and unapologetic call that we count every single vote.
sentences.zh: 我收回我的让步言论，并发出坚定且毫不妥协的呼吁，要求清点每一张选票。

sentences.en: In the Georgia governor's race between Democrat Stacey Abrams and Republican Brian Kemp, there is still no declared winner, with the votes expected to be counted until tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 在民主党人斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯和共和党人布莱恩·坎普之间的佐治亚州州长竞选中，目前仍未宣布获胜者，预计计票工作将持续到明天。

sentences.en: And the Times is reporting that last year, top Saudi intelligence officials close to the crown prince
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，去年，接近沙特王储的高级情报官员

sentences.en: explored the possibility of using private companies to assassinate Iranian enemies of the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 探讨了利用私营公司暗杀沙特在伊朗的敌人的可能性。

sentences.en: Coming months before the killing of the journalist Jamal Khashoggi, those talks indicate that Saudi officials have considered assassinations as a political tool
sentences.zh: 这些谈话发生在记者贾迈勒·卡舒吉遇害前几个月，表明沙特官员已将暗杀视为一种政治工具，

sentences.en: since the beginning of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's reign as he was first consolidating power.
sentences.zh: 这始于王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼统治初期，当时他正在巩固权力。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。
